source.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם לָבָ֜ן בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיְנַשֵּׁ֧ק לְבָנָ֛יו וְלִבְנוֹתָ֖יו וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶתְהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ וַיָּ֥שָׁב לָבָ֖ן לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early Laban in the morning and kissed his sons and his daughters and blessed them; and went and returned Laban to his place.

en.L: And Laban rose early in the morning and kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them. Then Laban departed and returned to his home.
en.B: Laban rose at dawn, kissed his grandchildren and his daughters, and gave them his blessing. Then he started back to his own home.
en.R: Laban got up early in the morning. He kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and asked God to bless them. Then he left to go home.

es.L: Y se levantó Labán muy de mañana, besó a sus nietos y a sus hijas y los bendijo. Luego Labán se fue y regresó a su casa.
es.B: Labán se levantó al amanecer, besó a sus nietos y a sus hijas, y les dio su bendición. Después emprendió el regreso a su casa.
es.R: Labán se levantó temprano por la mañana. Besó a sus nietos y a sus hijas, y le pidió a Dios que los bendijera. Luego se fue a su casa.

fr.L: Et Laban se leva de bon matin, embrassa ses petits-enfants et ses filles, et les bénit. Puis Laban s’en alla et retourna chez lui.
fr.B: Laban se leva à l’aube, embrassa ses petits-enfants et ses filles, et leur donna sa bénédiction. Puis il reprit le chemin de sa maison.
fr.R: Laban s’est levé tôt le matin. Il a embrassé ses petits-enfants et ses filles, et il a demandé à Dieu de les bénir. Puis il est reparti chez lui.

sw.L: Na Labani aliamka asubuhi na mapema, akawabusu wajukuu wake na binti zake, akawabariki. Kisha Labani akaondoka, akarudi nyumbani kwake.
sw.B: Labani aliamka alfajiri, akawabusu wajukuu wake na binti zake, akawapa baraka zake. Kisha akaanza safari ya kurudi nyumbani kwake.
sw.R: Labani aliamka mapema asubuhi. Akawabusu wajukuu wake na binti zake, akamwomba Mungu awabariki. Kisha akaondoka kwenda nyumbani.

decisions.choice: Verse numbers follow the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text this verse begins chapter 32, so every verse of the chapter is numbered one higher than in Bibles that number it 31:55 (32:1 here is 31:55 there; 32:33 here is 32:32 there). Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates.

decisions.choice: his sons: his grandchildren
decisions.reason: As in 31:28 and 31:43, "sons" means Laban's daughters' children. He gets the farewell kiss he said Jacob had denied him (31:28).

decisions.choice: grandchildren
decisions.reason: Every level says who the "sons" are, as Balanced did in 31:28 (m2).

decisions.choice: He asked God to bless them
decisions.reason: Readable says what blessing them meant: a farewell prayer for their good.

decisions.choice: passé simple at L and B ("se leva", "embrassa"); passé composé at R ("s'est levé", "a embrassé")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide has it: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative in French, used at Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the passé composé, the past tense of spoken and school French. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב הָלַ֣ךְ לְדַרְכּ֑וֹ וַיִּפְגְּעוּ־ב֖וֹ מַלְאֲכֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jacob went on his way, and met him [the] angels of God.

en.L: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
en.B: As Jacob continued on his journey, angels of God met him.
en.R: Jacob also continued on his way. Some of God's angels met him.

es.L: Y Jacob siguió su camino, y le salieron al encuentro los ángeles de Dios.
es.B: Mientras Jacob proseguía su viaje, unos ángeles de Dios le salieron al encuentro.
es.R: Jacob también siguió su camino. Algunos ángeles de Dios se encontraron con él.

fr.L: Et Jacob alla son chemin, et les anges de Dieu le rencontrèrent.
fr.B: Tandis que Jacob poursuivait sa route, des anges de Dieu vinrent à sa rencontre.
fr.R: Jacob, lui aussi, a continué sa route. Des anges de Dieu sont venus à sa rencontre.

sw.L: Na Yakobo akaenda njia yake, nao malaika wa Mungu wakakutana naye.
sw.B: Yakobo alipokuwa akiendelea na safari yake, malaika wa Mungu walikutana naye.
sw.R: Yakobo naye aliendelea na safari yake. Malaika kadhaa wa Mungu wakakutana naye.

decisions.choice: the angels of God: as at Bethel
decisions.reason: Jacob saw the angels of God going up and down at Bethel as he left the land (28:12). Now, as he returns, they meet him again. The visit frames his years away.

decisions.choice: met him: came upon him
decisions.reason: The verb (paga) means to meet or encounter, sometimes with hostile intent; here it is simply a meeting, perhaps a reassurance before meeting Esau.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאָ֔ם מַחֲנֵ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים זֶ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֛א שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מַֽחֲנָֽיִם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said Jacob when he saw them, [the] camp of God [is] this; and he called [the] name of that place Mahanaim.

en.L: And Jacob said when he saw them, "This is the camp of God!" And he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
en.B: At the sight of them Jacob said, "This is God's own camp!" and he called the place Mahanaim.
en.R: When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is God's camp!" So he named that place Mahanaim, which means "two camps."

es.L: Y dijo Jacob cuando los vio: «¡Este es el campamento de Dios!». Y llamó el nombre de aquel lugar Mahanaim.
es.B: Al verlos, Jacob dijo: «¡Este es el campamento del mismo Dios!», y llamó a aquel lugar Mahanaim.
es.R: Cuando Jacob los vio, dijo: «¡Este es el campamento de Dios!». Por eso le puso a ese lugar el nombre de Mahanaim, que significa «dos campamentos».

fr.L: Et Jacob dit, quand il les vit : « C’est ici le camp de Dieu ! » Et il appela le nom de ce lieu Mahanaïm.
fr.B: En les voyant, Jacob dit : « C’est le camp de Dieu lui-même ! » Et il nomma ce lieu Mahanaïm.
fr.R: Quand Jacob les a vus, il a dit : « C’est le camp de Dieu ! » Alors il a appelé cet endroit Mahanaïm, ce qui veut dire « deux camps ».

sw.L: Na Yakobo akasema alipowaona, "Hii ni kambi ya Mungu!" Akapaita jina la mahali pale Mahanaimu.
sw.B: Yakobo alipowaona alisema, "Hii ni kambi ya Mungu mwenyewe!" Akapaita mahali pale Mahanaimu.
sw.R: Yakobo alipowaona, alisema, "Hii ni kambi ya Mungu!" Kwa hiyo akapaita mahali pale Mahanaimu, maana yake "kambi mbili."

decisions.choice: Mahanaim: "two camps"
decisions.reason: The name is the dual form of machaneh, "camp". God's camp meets Jacob's; and Jacob will soon divide his own people into two camps (verses 8, 11). Mahanaim became a town east of the Jordan (2 Samuel 2:8).

decisions.choice: which means "two camps"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֤ב מַלְאָכִים֙ לְפָנָ֔יו אֶל־עֵשָׂ֖ו אָחִ֑יו אַ֥רְצָה שֵׂעִ֖יר שְׂדֵ֥ה אֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Jacob messengers before him to Esau his brother, to [the] land of Seir, [the] country of Edom.

en.L: And Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to Esau his brother in the land of Seir, the country of Edom,
en.B: Jacob then sent messengers ahead to his brother Esau, to the land of Seir in the region of Edom.
en.R: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau. Esau lived in the land of Seir, in the country of Edom.

es.L: Y envió Jacob mensajeros delante de sí a Esaú su hermano, a la tierra de Seír, el campo de Edom,
es.B: Luego Jacob envió mensajeros por delante a su hermano Esaú, a la tierra de Seír, en la región de Edom.
es.R: Jacob mandó mensajeros por delante a su hermano Esaú. Esaú vivía en la tierra de Seír, en el país de Edom.

fr.L: Et Jacob envoya des messagers devant lui vers Ésaü, son frère, au pays de Séir, la campagne d’Édom,
fr.B: Jacob envoya alors des messagers en avant, vers son frère Ésaü, au pays de Séir, dans la région d’Édom.
fr.R: Jacob a envoyé des messagers devant lui chez son frère Ésaü. Ésaü vivait dans le pays de Séir, dans le territoire d’Édom.

sw.L: Na Yakobo akatuma wajumbe mbele yake kwa Esau ndugu yake, katika nchi ya Seiri, nchi ya Edomu,
sw.B: Kisha Yakobo alituma wajumbe watangulie mbele yake kwa ndugu yake Esau, katika nchi ya Seiri, eneo la Edomu.
sw.R: Yakobo alituma wajumbe mbele yake kwa ndugu yake Esau. Esau aliishi katika nchi ya Seiri, katika nchi ya Edomu.

decisions.choice: messengers (mal'akhim): the same word as "angels"
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the angels in verse 2. Jacob, met by God's messengers, now sends his own.

decisions.choice: Seir, Edom: Esau's country
decisions.reason: Seir is the hill country south of the Dead Sea where Esau settled; its later name was Edom, "red", after Esau (25:30; 36:8).

source.text: וַיְצַ֤ו אֹתָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֔וּן לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לְעֵשָׂ֑ו כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ עַבְדְּךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב עִם־לָבָ֣ן גַּ֔רְתִּי וָאֵחַ֖ר עַד־עָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he commanded them, saying, thus you shall say to my lord, to Esau, thus says your servant Jacob: with Laban I have sojourned and stayed until now.

en.L: and he commanded them, saying, "Thus you shall say to my lord Esau: 'Thus says your servant Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban and stayed until now.
en.B: He instructed them, "Tell my lord Esau this: 'Your servant Jacob sends word: I have lived as a guest with Laban and stayed on there until now.
en.R: He told them to say this to Esau: "My master Esau, your servant Jacob sends you this message: I have been living with Laban all this time.

es.L: y les ordenó, diciendo: «Así {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}} a mi señor Esaú: “Así dice tu siervo Jacob: He vivido como extranjero con Labán y me he quedado hasta ahora.
es.B: Les dio estas instrucciones: «{{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} esto a mi señor Esaú: “Tu siervo Jacob te manda decir: He vivido como huésped en casa de Labán y me he quedado allí hasta ahora.
es.R: Les dijo que le dieran este mensaje a Esaú: «Mi señor Esaú, tu siervo Jacob te envía este mensaje: He estado viviendo con Labán todo este tiempo.

fr.L: et il leur commanda, disant : « Ainsi vous direz à mon seigneur Ésaü : “Ainsi parle ton serviteur Jacob : J’ai séjourné en étranger chez Laban, et je m’y suis attardé jusqu’à maintenant.
fr.B: Il leur donna cet ordre : « Voici ce que vous direz à mon seigneur Ésaü : “Ton serviteur Jacob te fait dire : J’ai vécu en hôte chez Laban, et j’y suis resté jusqu’à présent.
fr.R: Il leur a dit de transmettre ce message à Ésaü : « Mon maître Ésaü, ton serviteur Jacob t’envoie ce message : J’ai vécu chez Laban pendant tout ce temps.

sw.L: akawaamuru, akisema, "Hivi ndivyo mtakavyomwambia bwana wangu Esau: 'Hivi ndivyo asemavyo mtumishi wako Yakobo: Nimekaa ugenini kwa Labani, nikakawia huko mpaka sasa.
sw.B: Akawaagiza, "Mwambieni bwana wangu Esau hivi: 'Mtumishi wako Yakobo anakuletea habari hii: Nimeishi kama mgeni kwa Labani, nimekaa huko mpaka sasa.
sw.R: Aliwaambia wamwambie Esau maneno haya: "Bwana wangu Esau, mtumishi wako Yakobo anakutumia ujumbe huu: Nimekuwa nikiishi kwa Labani muda wote huu.

decisions.choice: my lord, your servant: the blessing turned around
decisions.reason: Isaac's blessing made Jacob lord over his brother (27:29, 37). Now Jacob calls Esau "my lord" and himself "your servant", seeking peace rather than claiming the blessing's first place.

decisions.choice: sojourned: lived as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) means to live in a place without belonging to it. Jacob presents himself as having been a guest abroad, not a rival at home.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי־לִי֙ שׁ֣וֹר וַחֲמ֔וֹר צֹ֖אן וְעֶ֣בֶד וְשִׁפְחָ֑ה וָֽאֶשְׁלְחָה֙ לְהַגִּ֣יד לַֽאדֹנִ֔י לִמְצֹא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And there is to me ox and donkey, flock and male slave and female slave; and I have sent to tell my lord, to find favor in your eyes.

en.L: And I have oxen and donkeys, flocks, male slaves and female slaves; and I have sent to tell my lord, in order to find favor in your eyes.'"
en.B: I own oxen and donkeys and flocks, and servants, men and women. I am sending to let my lord know, hoping you will look on me with favor.'"
en.R: I have cattle, donkeys, sheep, goats and servants. Master, I am sending this message to you so that you will be kind to me.'"

es.L: Y tengo bueyes y asnos, ovejas, esclavos y esclavas; y he enviado a avisar a mi señor, para hallar gracia ante tus ojos”».
es.B: Tengo bueyes, asnos y rebaños, y siervos y siervas. Envío este aviso a mi señor, con la esperanza de que me mires con favor”».
es.R: Tengo ganado, burros, ovejas, cabras y siervos. Señor mío, te mando este mensaje para que seas bueno conmigo».

fr.L: Et j’ai des bœufs et des ânes, du petit bétail, des esclaves hommes et des esclaves femmes ; et j’ai envoyé informer mon seigneur, afin de trouver grâce à tes yeux.” »
fr.B: Je possède des bœufs, des ânes, du petit bétail, des serviteurs et des servantes. J’envoie prévenir mon seigneur, dans l’espoir que tu me regardes avec bienveillance.” »
fr.R: J’ai des bœufs, des ânes, des moutons, des chèvres et des serviteurs. Mon maître, je t’envoie ce message pour que tu sois bon envers moi. »

sw.L: Nami nina ng'ombe na punda, kondoo na mbuzi, watumwa wa kiume na wa kike; nami nimetuma kumjulisha bwana wangu, ili nipate kibali machoni pako.'"
sw.B: Ninamiliki ng'ombe, punda na makundi ya kondoo na mbuzi, na watumishi wanaume na wanawake. Ninatuma habari hii kwa bwana wangu, nikitumaini utanitazama kwa fadhili.'"
sw.R: Nina ng'ombe, punda, kondoo, mbuzi na watumishi. Bwana wangu, ninakutumia ujumbe huu ili unitendee wema."

decisions.choice: oxen, donkeys, flocks, slaves: Jacob is not coming in need
decisions.reason: By listing his wealth Jacob shows that he has not come to claim his father's estate, and he hints that he can give gifts (verses 14-22).

decisions.choice: male and female slaves
decisions.reason: The words (eved, shifchah) are the usual words for owned servants (30:43).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servants" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּ֤אנוּ אֶל־אָחִ֨יךָ֙ אֶל־עֵשָׂ֔ו וְגַם֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ לִקְרָֽאתְךָ֔ וְאַרְבַּע־מֵא֥וֹת אִ֖ישׁ עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned the messengers to Jacob, saying, we came to your brother, to Esau, and also he [is] coming to meet you, and four hundred men [are] with him.

en.L: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, "We came to your brother Esau, and he is coming to meet you, and 400 men with him."
en.B: The messengers returned and told Jacob, "We reached your brother Esau. He is already coming out to meet you, with 400 men at his side."
en.R: The messengers came back. They told Jacob, "We found your brother Esau. He is coming toward you now, and 400 men are with him."

es.L: Y volvieron los mensajeros a Jacob, diciendo: «Fuimos a tu hermano, a Esaú, y él también viene a tu encuentro, y cuatrocientos hombres con él».
es.B: Los mensajeros volvieron y le dijeron a Jacob: «Llegamos hasta tu hermano Esaú. Ya viene a tu encuentro, y lo acompañan cuatrocientos hombres».
es.R: Los mensajeros regresaron. Le dijeron a Jacob: «Encontramos a tu hermano Esaú. Ahora viene hacia ti, y trae cuatrocientos hombres con él».

fr.L: Et les messagers revinrent vers Jacob, disant : « Nous sommes allés vers ton frère, vers Ésaü, et il vient lui aussi à ta rencontre, et quatre cents hommes avec lui. »
fr.B: Les messagers revinrent dire à Jacob : « Nous sommes arrivés chez ton frère Ésaü. Il vient déjà à ta rencontre, accompagné de quatre cents hommes. »
fr.R: Les messagers sont revenus. Ils ont dit à Jacob : « Nous avons trouvé ton frère Ésaü. Il est en train de venir vers toi, et quatre cents hommes sont avec lui. »

sw.L: Wale wajumbe wakarudi kwa Yakobo, wakisema, "Tulifika kwa ndugu yako, kwa Esau, naye pia anakuja kukulaki, na watu mia nne pamoja naye."
sw.B: Wajumbe walirudi, wakamwambia Yakobo, "Tulimfikia ndugu yako Esau. Tayari anakuja kukulaki, akiwa na watu mia nne."
sw.R: Wajumbe walirudi. Wakamwambia Yakobo, "Tulimkuta ndugu yako Esau. Sasa hivi anakuja kukutana nawe, na watu mia nne wako pamoja naye."

decisions.choice: four hundred men: a war band
decisions.reason: Four hundred men was the size of a raiding force (1 Samuel 22:2; 30:10, 17). The messengers report no message from Esau, so Jacob cannot tell what he intends. Esau had vowed to kill Jacob (27:41).

source.text: וַיִּירָ֧א יַעֲקֹ֛ב מְאֹ֖ד וַיֵּ֣צֶר ל֑וֹ וַיַּ֜חַץ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֗וֹ וְאֶת־הַצֹּ֧אן וְאֶת־הַבָּקָ֛ר וְהַגְּמַלִּ֖ים לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And was afraid Jacob greatly, and was distressed to him; and he divided the people who [were] with him, and the flock and the herd and the camels, into two camps.

en.L: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed. And he divided the people who were with him, and the flocks and herds and camels, into two camps.
en.B: Jacob was badly frightened and anxious. He divided his people into two camps, along with the flocks, the herds and the camels.
en.R: Jacob was very afraid and upset. So he divided his people into two groups. He also divided the sheep, goats, cattle and camels into two groups.

es.L: Entonces Jacob tuvo mucho miedo y se angustió. Y dividió en dos campamentos a la gente que estaba con él, y las ovejas, las vacas y los camellos.
es.B: Jacob sintió un gran temor y angustia. Repartió a su gente en dos campamentos, junto con las ovejas, las vacas y los camellos.
es.R: Jacob tuvo mucho miedo y se preocupó. Entonces dividió a su gente en dos grupos. También dividió en dos grupos las ovejas, las cabras, las vacas y los camellos.

fr.L: Alors Jacob eut très peur et fut dans l’angoisse. Et il partagea le peuple qui était avec lui, et le petit bétail, le gros bétail et les chameaux, en deux camps.
fr.B: Jacob fut saisi de frayeur et d’angoisse. Il répartit ses gens en deux camps, ainsi que le petit et le gros bétail et les chameaux.
fr.R: Jacob a eu très peur, et il était inquiet. Alors il a divisé ses gens en deux groupes. Il a aussi divisé les moutons, les chèvres, les vaches et les chameaux en deux groupes.

sw.L: Ndipo Yakobo akaogopa sana, akafadhaika. Akagawanya watu waliokuwa pamoja naye, na kondoo na ng'ombe na ngamia, kuwa kambi mbili.
sw.B: Yakobo aliogopa mno, akahangaika. Akawagawanya watu wake katika kambi mbili, pamoja na makundi ya kondoo na mbuzi, ng'ombe na ngamia.
sw.R: Yakobo aliogopa sana, akasumbuka moyoni. Kwa hiyo akawagawanya watu wake katika makundi mawili. Akagawanya pia kondoo, mbuzi, ng'ombe na ngamia katika makundi mawili.

decisions.choice: two camps: the name Mahanaim again
decisions.reason: The words are those of the place name in verse 3. Where God's camp met him, Jacob's fear makes two camps of his own.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אִם־יָב֥וֹא עֵשָׂ֛ו אֶל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הָאַחַ֖ת וְהִכָּ֑הוּ וְהָיָ֛ה הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הַנִּשְׁאָ֖ר לִפְלֵיטָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, if comes Esau to the one camp and attacks it, then will be the camp that remains for escape.

en.L: For he said, "If Esau comes to the one camp and strikes it, then the camp that is left will escape."
en.B: His thought was, "If Esau falls on one camp and strikes it, the camp that is left will be able to escape."
en.R: He thought, "Esau may attack one group. If he does, the other group can run away."

es.L: Porque dijo: «Si Esaú viene a un campamento y lo ataca, el campamento que quede escapará».
es.B: Pensaba: «Si Esaú cae sobre un campamento y lo ataca, el campamento que quede podrá escapar».
es.R: Pensó: «Puede que Esaú ataque a un grupo. Si lo hace, el otro grupo podrá huir».

fr.L: Car il dit : « Si Ésaü vient à l’un des camps et le frappe, alors le camp qui restera en réchappera. »
fr.B: Il pensait : « Si Ésaü tombe sur un camp et l’attaque, le camp qui reste pourra s’échapper. »
fr.R: Il s’est dit : « Ésaü va peut-être attaquer un groupe. Dans ce cas, l’autre groupe pourra s’enfuir. »

sw.L: Kwa maana alisema, "Esau akija kwenye kambi moja na kuipiga, basi kambi itakayobaki itaokoka."
sw.B: Aliwaza, "Esau akiivamia kambi moja na kuishambulia, kambi itakayobaki itaweza kuokoka."
sw.R: Alifikiri, "Huenda Esau atashambulia kundi moja. Akifanya hivyo, kundi lingine litaweza kukimbia."

decisions.choice: he said: he thought
decisions.reason: "Said" here means said to himself, as often (26:9).

decisions.choice: His thought was (B); He thought (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "said" here (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ יַעֲקֹב֒ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אָבִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם וֵאלֹהֵ֖י אָבִ֣י יִצְחָ֑ק יְהוָ֞ה הָאֹמֵ֣ר אֵלַ֗י שׁ֧וּב לְאַרְצְךָ֛ וּלְמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֖ וְאֵיטִ֥יבָה עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jacob, God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, YHWH, who said to me, return to your land and to your kindred, and I will do good with you,

en.L: And Jacob said, "O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, who said to me, 'Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will do you good,'
en.B: And Jacob prayed: "God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, it was {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who said to me, 'Return to your land and your family, and I will make things go well for you.'
en.R: Then Jacob prayed, "God of my grandfather Abraham and of my father Isaac, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told me, 'Go back to your own land and your own family, and I will be good to you.'

es.L: Y dijo Jacob: «Oh Dios de mi padre Abraham y Dios de mi padre Isaac, oh {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que me dijiste: “Vuelve a tu tierra y a tu parentela, y te haré bien”,
es.B: Y Jacob oró: «Dios de mi padre Abraham, Dios de mi padre Isaac, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, fuiste {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien me dijo: “Vuelve a tu tierra y a tu familia, y haré que te vaya bien”.
es.R: Entonces Jacob oró: «Dios de mi abuelo Abraham y de mi padre Isaac, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me dijiste: “Regresa a tu tierra y con tu familia, y yo seré bueno contigo”.

fr.L: Et Jacob dit : « Ô Dieu de mon père Abraham et Dieu de mon père Isaac, ô {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui m’as dit : “Retourne dans ton pays et vers ta parenté, et je te ferai du bien”,
fr.B: Et Jacob pria : « Dieu de mon père Abraham, Dieu de mon père Isaac, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui m’as dit : “Retourne dans ton pays et dans ta famille, et je ferai que tout aille bien pour toi.”
fr.R: Puis Jacob a prié : « Dieu de mon grand-père Abraham et de mon père Isaac, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as dit : “Rentre dans ton pays, auprès de ta famille, et je serai bon pour toi.”

sw.L: Na Yakobo akasema, "Ee Mungu wa baba yangu Abrahamu, na Mungu wa baba yangu Isaka, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uliyeniambia, 'Rudi katika nchi yako na kwa jamaa zako, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakutendea mema,'
sw.B: Yakobo akaomba, "Mungu wa baba yangu Abrahamu, Mungu wa baba yangu Isaka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ni {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyeniambia, 'Rudi katika nchi yako na kwa jamaa yako, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakufanikisha.'
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo akaomba, "Mungu wa babu yangu Abrahamu na wa baba yangu Isaka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliniambia, 'Rudi katika nchi yako na kwa jamaa yako, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakuwa mwema kwako.'

decisions.choice: Jacob's prayer: the first long prayer in the Bible
decisions.reason: Jacob calls on God by the names of his relationship with Abraham and Isaac and by his own name, the LORD. He reminds God of his command (31:3, 13) and his promise (28:15), confesses his unworthiness (verse 11), asks for rescue (verse 12) and holds God to his word (verse 13). It is a pattern later prayers follow.

decisions.choice: I will do you good: I will deal well with you
decisions.reason: The verb (yatav) means to make things go well for someone. God had said "I will be with you" (31:3); Jacob takes it as a promise of good.

decisions.choice: LORD (divine name setting, addressed)
decisions.reason: When God is addressed by his name, the divine name has no article: "LORD", or "Yahweh" under the setting.

decisions.choice: it was you who said to me (B); you told me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the relative clause into a clause addressed to God, so "you" takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, with no article
decisions.reason: Jacob addresses God by name, so, as the English "O LORD", the span has no article: "SEÑOR", or "Yahvé" under the setting.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, with no article
decisions.reason: Jacob addresses God by name, so, as the English "O LORD", the span has no article: "SEIGNEUR", or "Yahvé" under the setting.

source.text: קָטֹ֜נְתִּי מִכֹּ֤ל הַחֲסָדִים֙ וּמִכָּל־הָ֣אֱמֶ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֣י בְמַקְלִ֗י עָבַ֨רְתִּי֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה וְעַתָּ֥ה הָיִ֖יתִי לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: I am too small for all the loyalties and all the faithfulness which you have done with your servant; for with my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.

en.L: I am not worthy of all the steadfast love and all the faithfulness that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown to your servant, for with only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
en.B: I am far too small for all the steadfast love and faithfulness {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown your servant. I had only a staff in my hand when I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
en.R: I do not deserve all the kindness {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown me. I do not deserve how faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been to me, your servant. When I crossed the Jordan River long ago, all I had was my walking stick. But now I have so much that I could divide it into two groups.

es.L: Soy demasiado pequeño para todo el amor fiel y toda la lealtad que has mostrado a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo; porque con solo mi cayado pasé este Jordán, y ahora he llegado a ser dos campamentos.
es.B: Soy muy poca cosa para tanto amor fiel y tanta lealtad como {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has mostrado a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo. Solo tenía un cayado en la mano cuando crucé este Jordán, y ahora he llegado a formar dos campamentos.
es.R: No merezco toda la bondad que me has mostrado. No merezco que hayas sido tan fiel conmigo, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo. Cuando crucé el río Jordán hace mucho tiempo, lo único que tenía era mi bastón. Pero ahora tengo tanto que lo he podido dividir en dos grupos.

fr.L: Je suis trop petit pour tout l’amour fidèle et toute la loyauté dont {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as usé envers {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur ; car avec mon seul bâton j’ai passé ce Jourdain, et maintenant je suis devenu deux camps.
fr.B: Je suis bien trop petit pour tout l’amour fidèle et toute la loyauté dont {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as entouré {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur. Je n’avais qu’un bâton à la main quand j’ai traversé ce Jourdain, et maintenant je forme deux camps.
fr.R: Je ne mérite pas toute la bonté que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as montrée. Je ne mérite pas que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sois si fidèle envers moi, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur. Quand j’ai traversé le Jourdain, il y a longtemps, je n’avais que mon bâton de marche. Mais maintenant, j’ai tant de biens que j’ai pu les partager en deux groupes.

sw.L: Mimi ni mdogo mno mbele ya upendo wote usiokoma na uaminifu wote ulionionyesha mimi mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}; kwa maana nilivuka Yordani hii nikiwa na fimbo yangu tu, na sasa nimekuwa kambi mbili.
sw.B: Mimi ni mdogo kabisa mbele ya upendo usiokoma na uaminifu huu wote ulionionyesha mimi mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Nilipovuka Yordani hii nilikuwa na fimbo tu mkononi, na sasa nimekuwa kambi mbili.
sw.R: Sistahili wema wote ulionitendea. Sistahili uaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwangu, mimi mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Nilipovuka mto Yordani zamani, nilikuwa na fimbo yangu ya kutembelea tu. Lakini sasa nina mali nyingi kiasi kwamba nimeweza kuigawanya katika makundi mawili.

decisions.choice: steadfast love and faithfulness (chesed, emet)
decisions.reason: The two words often go together of God (24:27; Exodus 34:6). Chesed is loyal, generous love that keeps a bond; emet is reliability, truth to one's word. Here the plural chasadim means many acts of such love.

decisions.choice: I am not worthy: literally "I am small"
decisions.reason: Jacob says he is "small" compared with God's kindness, too insignificant to have earned it.

decisions.choice: with only my staff ... two camps
decisions.reason: Jacob fled from Esau with nothing but a walking staff (28:10). Twenty years later he is rich enough to form two camps (verse 8), a sign of the good God promised.

decisions.choice: you (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: "You" addressed to God takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: el amor fiel y la lealtad
alternatives: el amor fiel y la fidelidad
decisions.reason: Chesed is "amor fiel" as settled for the Pentateuch; emet is given as "lealtad" so that "fiel ... fidelidad" does not repeat the same word for two Hebrew words.

decisions.choice: l'amour fidèle et la loyauté
decisions.reason: Chesed is "l'amour fidèle" as settled for the Pentateuch; emet is given as "la loyauté" so that "fidèle ... fidélité" does not repeat the same word for two Hebrew words.

source.text: הַצִּילֵ֥נִי נָ֛א מִיַּ֥ד אָחִ֖י מִיַּ֣ד עֵשָׂ֑ו כִּֽי־יָרֵ֤א אָנֹכִי֙ אֹת֔וֹ פֶּן־יָב֣וֹא וְהִכַּ֔נִי אֵ֖ם עַל־בָּנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Deliver me please from [the] hand of my brother, from [the] hand of Esau; for fearing [am] I him, lest he come and strike me, mother with children.

en.L: Deliver me, please, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I fear him, that he may come and strike me down, the mothers with the children.
en.B: Rescue me from my brother, from Esau's hand. I fear that he will come and strike us all down, mothers and children together.
en.R: Please save me from my brother Esau. I am afraid he will come and kill me and all my wives and children.

es.L: Líbrame, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ruego, de la mano de mi hermano, de la mano de Esaú, porque yo le temo, no sea que venga y me hiera, a las madres con los hijos.
es.B: Rescátame de mi hermano, de la mano de Esaú. Temo que venga y acabe con todos nosotros, madres e hijos por igual.
es.R: Por favor, sálvame de mi hermano Esaú. Tengo miedo de que venga y nos mate a mí y a todas mis mujeres y a mis hijos.

fr.L: Délivre-moi, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} prie, de la main de mon frère, de la main d’Ésaü, car je le crains, de peur qu’il ne vienne et ne me frappe, les mères avec les enfants.
fr.B: Arrache-moi à mon frère, à la main d’Ésaü. J’ai peur qu’il vienne nous frapper tous, les mères comme les enfants.
fr.R: Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} prie, sauve-moi de mon frère Ésaü. J’ai peur qu’il vienne me tuer, avec toutes mes femmes et mes enfants.

sw.L: Uniokoe, nakuomba, kutoka mkononi mwa ndugu yangu, kutoka mkononi mwa Esau; kwa maana mimi ninamwogopa, asije akanipiga, akina mama pamoja na watoto.
sw.B: Uniokoe na ndugu yangu, na mkono wa Esau. Ninaogopa atakuja kutuangamiza sote, akina mama pamoja na watoto.
sw.R: Tafadhali niokoe kutoka kwa ndugu yangu Esau. Ninaogopa atakuja kuniua mimi na wake zangu wote na watoto.

decisions.choice: the mothers with the children: everyone, without mercy
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures a slaughter that spares no one, not even women and children (Hosea 10:14).

decisions.choice: from the hand of: from the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֔רְתָּ הֵיטֵ֥ב אֵיטִ֖יב עִמָּ֑ךְ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, you said, surely I will do good with you, and I will make your offspring like [the] sand of the sea, which not can be counted for multitude.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said, 'I will surely do you good, and make your offspring like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted for multitude.'"
en.B: Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} said, 'I will surely make things go well for you, and I will make your descendants like the sand of the sea, beyond counting for their number.'"
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised me, 'I will surely be good to you. I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them. They will be like the sand on the seashore.'"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} dijiste: “Ciertamente te haré bien, y haré tu descendencia como la arena del mar, que no se puede contar por su multitud”».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} mismo dijiste: “Ciertamente haré que te vaya bien, y haré que tus descendientes sean como la arena del mar, tantos que no se pueden contar”».
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me prometiste: “Seguro que seré bueno contigo. Te daré tantos descendientes que nadie los podrá contar. Serán como la arena de la playa”».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit : “Je te ferai sûrement du bien, et je rendrai ta descendance comme le sable de la mer, qu’on ne peut compter tant il est nombreux.” »
fr.B: Et c’est bien {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui as dit : “Je ferai sûrement que tout aille bien pour toi, et je rendrai tes descendants comme le sable de la mer, si nombreux qu’on ne peut les compter.” »
fr.R: Mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as fait cette promesse : “C’est sûr, je serai bon pour toi. Je te donnerai tant de descendants que personne ne pourra les compter. Ils seront comme le sable au bord de la mer.” »

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulisema, 'Hakika nitakutendea mema, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitaufanya uzao wako kama mchanga wa bahari, usioweza kuhesabika kwa wingi wake.'"
sw.B: Tena {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ulisema, 'Hakika nitakufanikisha, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawafanya wazao wako kama mchanga wa bahari, wasioweza kuhesabika kwa wingi wao.'"
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliniahidi, 'Hakika nitakuwa mwema kwako. Nitakupa wazao wengi sana hata hakuna mtu atakayeweza kuwahesabu. Watakuwa kama mchanga wa ufuoni mwa bahari.'"

decisions.choice: like the sand of the sea: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: God swore to make Abraham's offspring like the sand of the seashore (22:17). To Jacob he spoke of the dust of the earth (28:14). Jacob holds God to the family promise.

decisions.choice: offspring (L), descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, zera is "offspring" in Literal and "descendants" in Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: you (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: "You" addressed to God takes the deity pronoun setting.

source.text: וַיָּ֥לֶן שָׁ֖ם בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִן־הַבָּ֧א בְיָד֛וֹ מִנְחָ֖ה לְעֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spent the night there that night, and he took from what had come into his hand a gift for Esau his brother:

en.L: And he spent the night there that night, and took from what he had with him a present for Esau his brother:
en.B: After spending the night there, he chose from his possessions a present for his brother Esau:
en.R: Jacob stayed there that night. He chose some of his animals as a gift for his brother Esau.

es.L: Y pasó allí aquella noche, y tomó de lo que tenía consigo un presente para Esaú su hermano:
es.B: Después de pasar allí la noche, escogió de entre sus bienes un regalo para su hermano Esaú:
es.R: Jacob se quedó allí esa noche. Escogió algunos de sus animales para regalárselos a su hermano Esaú.

fr.L: Et il passa la nuit là, cette nuit-là, et il prit de ce qu’il avait avec lui un présent pour Ésaü, son frère :
fr.B: Après avoir passé la nuit en ce lieu, il choisit parmi ses biens un présent pour son frère Ésaü :
fr.R: Jacob est resté là pour la nuit. Il a choisi une partie de ses animaux pour en faire un cadeau à son frère Ésaü.

sw.L: Akalala pale usiku ule, akatwaa katika vitu alivyokuwa navyo zawadi kwa Esau ndugu yake:
sw.B: Baada ya kulala pale usiku, alichagua katika mali zake zawadi kwa ajili ya ndugu yake Esau:
sw.R: Yakobo alilala pale usiku ule. Alichagua baadhi ya wanyama wake wawe zawadi kwa ndugu yake Esau.

decisions.choice: a present (minchah): a gift or tribute
decisions.reason: The word minchah is used for a gift to win favor, for tribute paid to a ruler, and later for a grain offering to God. It sounds like machaneh, "camp" (verses 3, 8, 22), and the chapter plays on the two.

decisions.choice: what he had with him: literally "what had come into his hand"
decisions.reason: The phrase means his possessions, what he had acquired.

source.text: עִזִּ֣ים מָאתַ֔יִם וּתְיָשִׁ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֑ים רְחֵלִ֥ים מָאתַ֖יִם וְאֵילִ֥ים עֶשְׂרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Female goats two hundred and male goats twenty, ewes two hundred and rams twenty,

en.L: 200 female goats and twenty male goats, 200 ewes and twenty rams,
en.B: 200 female goats and twenty male goats, 200 ewes and twenty rams,
en.R: 200 female goats and twenty male goats, 200 female sheep and twenty rams,

es.L: 200 cabras y veinte machos cabríos, 200 ovejas y veinte carneros,
es.B: 200 cabras y veinte machos cabríos, 200 ovejas y veinte carneros,
es.R: 200 cabras y veinte chivos, 200 ovejas y veinte carneros,

fr.L: 200 chèvres et vingt boucs, 200 brebis et vingt béliers,
fr.B: 200 chèvres et vingt boucs, 200 brebis et vingt béliers,
fr.R: 200 chèvres et vingt boucs, 200 moutons femelles et vingt béliers,

sw.L: mbuzi jike 200 na mabeberu ishirini, kondoo jike 200 na kondoo dume ishirini,
sw.B: mbuzi jike 200 na mabeberu ishirini, kondoo jike 200 na kondoo dume ishirini,
sw.R: mbuzi wa kike 200 na mbuzi dume ishirini, kondoo wa kike 200 na kondoo dume ishirini,

decisions.choice: a generous gift arranged for breeding
decisions.reason: The ratio of one male to ten females was a good proportion for breeding herds. The gift totals 550 animals, a large fortune.

source.text: גְּמַלִּ֧ים מֵינִיק֛וֹת וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשִׁ֑ים פָּר֤וֹת אַרְבָּעִים֙ וּפָרִ֣ים עֲשָׂרָ֔ה אֲתֹנֹ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וַעְיָרִ֖םעֲשָׂרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: camels nursing and their young thirty, cows forty and bulls ten, female donkeys twenty and male donkeys ten.

en.L: thirty milking camels and their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.
en.B: thirty camels with their nursing young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.
en.R: thirty female camels with their babies, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

es.L: treinta camellas que amamantaban, con sus crías, cuarenta vacas y diez toros, veinte asnas y diez asnos.
es.B: treinta camellas con sus crías de leche, cuarenta vacas y diez toros, veinte burras y diez burros.
es.R: treinta camellas con sus crías, cuarenta vacas y diez toros, veinte burras y diez burros.

fr.L: trente chamelles qui allaitent, avec leurs petits, quarante vaches et dix taureaux, vingt ânesses et dix ânes.
fr.B: trente chamelles avec les petits qu’elles allaitaient, quarante vaches et dix taureaux, vingt ânesses et dix ânes.
fr.R: trente chamelles et leurs petits, quarante vaches et dix taureaux, vingt ânesses et dix ânes.

sw.L: ngamia thelathini wanaonyonyesha pamoja na wana wao, ng'ombe jike arobaini na mafahali kumi, punda jike ishirini na punda dume kumi.
sw.B: ngamia jike thelathini pamoja na watoto wao wanaonyonya, ng'ombe arobaini na mafahali kumi, punda jike ishirini na punda dume kumi.
sw.R: ngamia jike thelathini pamoja na watoto wao, ng'ombe arobaini na mafahali kumi, punda jike ishirini na punda dume kumi.

decisions.choice: milking camels: the most valuable animals
decisions.reason: Female camels with young gave milk and more camels; they were the costliest part of the gift.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֙ בְּיַד־עֲבָדָ֔יו עֵ֥דֶר עֵ֖דֶר לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַ֤יֹּאמֶר אֶל־עֲבָדָיו֙ עִבְר֣וּ לְפָנַ֔י וְרֶ֣וַח תָּשִׂ֔ימוּ בֵּ֥ין עֵ֖דֶר וּבֵ֥ין עֵֽדֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave [them] into [the] hand of his servants, each herd by itself, and he said to his servants, pass on before me, and a space put between herd and between herd.

en.L: And he put them in the charge of his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants, "Go on ahead of me, and put a space between drove and drove."
en.B: He handed them over to his servants, one drove at a time, and told them, "Cross ahead of me, and leave a gap between each drove and the next."
en.R: He gave each group of animals to one of his servants. He told them, "Go ahead of me. Keep some space between the groups."

es.L: Y los entregó en mano de sus siervos, cada manada aparte, y dijo a sus siervos: «{{plural_you:Pasen|Pasad}} delante de mí, y {{plural_you:pongan|poned}} espacio entre manada y manada».
es.B: Los entregó a sus siervos, manada por manada, y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Crucen|Cruzad}} delante de mí, y {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} una distancia entre una manada y la siguiente».
es.R: Le dio cada grupo de animales a uno de sus siervos. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} delante de mí. {{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} un espacio entre los grupos».

fr.L: Et il les remit entre les mains de ses serviteurs, chaque troupeau à part, et il dit à ses serviteurs : « Passez devant moi, et mettez un espace entre troupeau et troupeau. »
fr.B: Il les confia à ses serviteurs, un troupeau après l’autre, et leur dit : « Passez devant moi, et laissez un intervalle entre chaque troupeau et le suivant. »
fr.R: Il a donné chaque groupe d’animaux à l’un de ses serviteurs. Il leur a dit : « Allez devant moi. Laissez de l’espace entre les groupes. »

sw.L: Akawatia mikononi mwa watumishi wake, kila kundi peke yake, akawaambia watumishi wake, "Vukeni mbele yangu, mkaweke nafasi kati ya kundi na kundi."
sw.B: Aliwakabidhi watumishi wake, kundi moja baada ya jingine, akawaambia, "Vukeni mbele yangu, na acheni nafasi kati ya kundi moja na jingine."
sw.R: Alimpa kila mtumishi kundi moja la wanyama. Akawaambia, "Tangulieni mbele yangu. Acheni nafasi kati ya makundi."

decisions.choice: a space between droves: one gift after another
decisions.reason: Sending the gift in separate droves meant Esau would meet one gift after another, each with the same message (verses 18-21), so that his anger might be worn down step by step.

decisions.choice: servants: slaves
decisions.reason: The word (eved) is the one used of the slaves in verse 6; these are men of Jacob's household.

es.R: Le dijo al siervo que iba delante: «Mi hermano Esaú se encontrará contigo. Te preguntará: “¿Quién es tu amo? ¿Adónde vas? ¿De quién son estos animales?”.

fr.B: Au serviteur de tête il dit : « Mon frère Ésaü va te rencontrer et te demander : “À qui appartiens-tu ? Où vas-tu ? Et à qui sont ces bêtes que tu conduis ?”

decisions.choice: To whom do you belong?: who is your master?
decisions.reason: The question asks whose servant the man is.

decisions.choice: the first: the servant with the first drove
decisions.reason: "The first" is the first of the servants driving the herds.

decisions.choice: your servant ... my lord: the language of a vassal
decisions.reason: The servants are to speak of Jacob as Esau's servant and of Esau as their lord. A minchah, "gift", was what an inferior sent a superior (43:11; Judges 3:15).

en.B: He gave the same command to the second, to the third, and to everyone who walked behind the droves: "This is what you are to tell Esau when you come upon him.
en.R: He gave the same orders to the second servant, the third servant and all the others who were driving the animals. He said, "When you meet Esau, say the same thing to him.

es.B: Dio la misma orden al segundo, al tercero y a todos los que iban detrás de las manadas: «Esto es lo que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que decirle a Esaú cuando {{plural_you:se encuentren|os encontréis}} con él.
es.R: Les dio las mismas órdenes al segundo siervo, al tercero y a todos los demás que llevaban los animales. Les dijo: «Cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} a Esaú, {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}} lo mismo.

fr.L: Et il commanda aussi au deuxième, et au troisième, et à tous ceux qui suivaient les troupeaux, disant : « C’est de cette manière que vous parlerez à Ésaü quand vous le trouverez,

sw.B: Akatoa agizo hilo hilo kwa wa pili, kwa wa tatu, na kwa wote waliotembea nyuma ya makundi: "Haya ndiyo mtakayomwambia Esau mtakapokutana naye.
sw.R: Akatoa maagizo hayo hayo kwa mtumishi wa pili, wa tatu na wengine wote waliokuwa wakiswaga wanyama. Akasema, "Mkikutana na Esau, mwambieni maneno hayo hayo.

source.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם גַּ֗ם הִנֵּ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אַחֲרֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־אָמַ֞ר אֲכַפְּרָ֣ה פָנָ֗יו בַּמִּנְחָה֙ הַהֹלֶ֣כֶת לְפָנָ֔י וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ אֶרְאֶ֣ה פָנָ֔יו אוּלַ֖י יִשָּׂ֥א פָנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you shall say, also behold, your servant Jacob [is] behind us; for he said, I will cover his face with the gift going before me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will lift up my face.

en.L: and you shall say, 'Look, your servant Jacob is behind us.'" For he thought, "I will appease him with the present that goes ahead of me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me."
en.B: Add this: 'Your servant Jacob is right behind us.'" His plan was, "I will win him over with the present that goes ahead of me, and then I will meet him face to face. It may be that he will receive me kindly."
en.R: Be sure to say, 'Your servant Jacob is coming behind us.'" Jacob thought, "These gifts that I am sending ahead will make Esau less angry. Then when I meet him, maybe he will forgive me."

es.L: y {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “He aquí, tu siervo Jacob [viene] detrás de nosotros”». Porque pensaba: «Lo apaciguaré con el presente que va delante de mí, y después veré su rostro; quizá me acepte».
es.B: {{plural_you:Añadan|Añadid}} esto: “Tu siervo Jacob viene justo detrás de nosotros”». Porque su plan era: «Me lo ganaré con el regalo que va delante de mí, y luego me presentaré ante él cara a cara. Puede que me reciba con bondad».
es.R: No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} de decirle: “Tu siervo Jacob viene detrás de nosotros”». Jacob pensaba: «Estos regalos que envío por delante harán que a Esaú se le pase el enojo. Luego, cuando me encuentre con él, tal vez me perdone».

fr.L: et vous direz : “Voici, ton serviteur Jacob [vient] derrière nous.” » Car il pensait : « Je l’apaiserai par le présent qui va devant moi, et ensuite je verrai sa face ; peut-être m’accueillera-t-il. »
fr.B: Ajoutez ceci : “Ton serviteur Jacob vient juste derrière nous.” » Car il se disait : « Je vais le gagner par le présent qui me précède ; ensuite, je le verrai face à face. Peut-être me fera-t-il bon accueil. »
fr.R: Surtout, dites-lui : “Ton serviteur Jacob arrive derrière nous.” » Jacob pensait : « Ces cadeaux que j’envoie devant moi vont calmer la colère d’Ésaü. Ensuite, quand je le rencontrerai, il me pardonnera peut-être. »

sw.L: na mtasema, 'Tazama, mtumishi wako Yakobo yuko nyuma yetu.'" Kwa maana alifikiri, "Nitamtuliza kwa zawadi inayotangulia mbele yangu, na baadaye nitauona uso wake; huenda atanikubali."
sw.B: Ongezeni na haya: 'Mtumishi wako Yakobo yuko nyuma yetu hapa.'" Mpango wake ulikuwa huu: "Nitamvuta kwa zawadi inayonitangulia, kisha nitaonana naye uso kwa uso. Huenda atanipokea kwa wema."
sw.R: Hakikisheni mnasema, 'Mtumishi wako Yakobo anakuja nyuma yetu.'" Yakobo aliwaza, "Zawadi hizi ninazotuma mbele zitapunguza hasira ya Esau. Kisha nikikutana naye, labda atanisamehe."

decisions.choice: I will appease him: literally "I will cover his face"
decisions.reason: The verb (kipper) is the one later used for atonement, covering or wiping away an offense. To "cover the face" of someone wronged is to pacify him, so he no longer sees the wrong (Proverbs 16:14).

decisions.choice: face: four times in two verses
decisions.reason: Jacob will "cover his face", "see his face" and hope Esau will "lift up my face", that is, receive him kindly (19:21). The gift passes "before his face" (verse 22). The word (panim) prepares for Peniel, "face of God" (verse 31), and for Jacob's words to Esau in 33:10.

decisions.choice: he will accept me: literally "he will lift up my face"
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to look with favor on a person who bows down before you, to accept him.

decisions.choice: appease him ... accept me (L); win him over ... receive me kindly (B); make Esau less angry ... forgive me (R)
alternatives: cover his face ... lift up my face
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense of the two idioms (m1, m3); the decisions show the Hebrew pictures.

source.text: וַתַּעֲבֹ֥ר הַמִּנְחָ֖ה עַל־פָּנָ֑יו וְה֛וּא לָ֥ן בַּלַּֽיְלָה־הַה֖וּא בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And passed on the gift before him, and he spent the night in that night in the camp.

en.L: So the present went on ahead of him, and he himself spent that night in the camp.
en.B: So the gift went on ahead of him, while he stayed the night in the camp.
en.R: The gifts went on ahead, but Jacob spent that night in the camp.

es.L: Y pasó el presente delante de él, y él pasó aquella noche en el campamento.
es.B: Así que el regalo se adelantó, mientras él se quedaba a pasar la noche en el campamento.
es.R: Los regalos se fueron por delante, pero Jacob pasó esa noche en el campamento.

fr.L: Et le présent passa devant lui, et lui passa cette nuit-là dans le camp.
fr.B: Le présent partit donc en avant, tandis que lui resta pour la nuit au camp.
fr.R: Les cadeaux sont partis en avant, mais Jacob a passé cette nuit-là au camp.

sw.L: Basi ile zawadi ikavuka mbele yake, naye mwenyewe akalala usiku ule kambini.
sw.B: Hivyo zawadi ilitangulia mbele yake, wakati yeye alilala usiku ule kambini.
sw.R: Zawadi zilitangulia, lakini Yakobo alilala kambini usiku ule.

decisions.choice: the present ... the camp: minchah and machaneh
decisions.reason: The two words sound alike, and the chapter places them side by side: the gift goes ahead, Jacob stays in the camp.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם׀בַּלַּ֣יְלָה ה֗וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֤י נָשָׁיו֙ וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י שִׁפְחֹתָ֔יו וְאֶת־אַחַ֥ד עָשָׂ֖ר יְלָדָ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֔ר אֵ֖ת מַעֲבַ֥ר יַבֹּֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And he arose in that night and took his two wives and his two slave women and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of [the] Jabbok.

en.L: And he arose that night and took his two wives, his two slave women and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
en.B: During that night he rose, took his two wives, his two female servants and his eleven sons, and crossed at the ford of the Jabbok.
en.R: During the night, Jacob got up. He took his two wives, his two female servants and his eleven sons across the Jabbok River where it was shallow.

es.L: Y se levantó aquella noche, y tomó a sus dos mujeres, sus dos esclavas y sus once hijos, y cruzó el vado del Jaboc.
es.B: Durante aquella noche se levantó, tomó a sus dos esposas, a sus dos siervas y a sus once hijos, y cruzó por el vado del Jaboc.
es.R: Durante la noche, Jacob se levantó. Llevó a sus dos esposas, a sus dos siervas y a sus once hijos al otro lado del río Jaboc, por un lugar poco profundo.

fr.L: Et il se leva cette nuit-là, prit ses deux femmes, ses deux esclaves et ses onze fils, et passa le gué du Jabbok.
fr.B: Pendant cette nuit-là, il se leva, prit ses deux femmes, ses deux servantes et ses onze fils, et passa le gué du Jabbok.
fr.R: Pendant la nuit, Jacob s’est levé. Il a fait traverser le Jabbok à ses deux femmes, à ses deux servantes et à ses onze fils, à un endroit où l’eau était peu profonde.

sw.L: Akaondoka usiku ule, akawachukua wake zake wawili, na wajakazi wake wawili, na wana wake kumi na mmoja, akavuka kivuko cha Yaboki.
sw.B: Usiku ule aliamka, akawachukua wake zake wawili, watumishi wake wawili wa kike na wana wake kumi na mmoja, akavuka kwenye kivuko cha Yaboki.
sw.R: Usiku ule Yakobo aliamka. Akawavusha wake zake wawili, watumishi wake wawili wa kike na wana wake kumi na mmoja ng'ambo ya mto Yaboki, mahali ambapo maji yalikuwa machache.

decisions.choice: Jabbok: a pun on Jacob and "wrestled"
decisions.reason: The river's name (yabboq) sounds like Jacob (ya'aqov) and like the verb "wrestled" (ye'aveq) in verse 25. The Jabbok flows west into the Jordan through Gilead.

decisions.choice: eleven sons
decisions.reason: Benjamin is not yet born (35:18). Jacob's daughter Dinah (30:21) is not counted with the sons but is surely with them.

decisions.choice: slave women: Bilhah and Zilpah
decisions.reason: The word (shifchah) is the one used of them in 29:24, 29.

decisions.choice: female servants
decisions.reason: "Female servants" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m3) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיִּקָּחֵ֔ם וַיַּֽעֲבִרֵ֖ם אֶת־הַנָּ֑חַל וַֽיַּעֲבֵ֖ר אֶת־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took them and sent them across the wadi, and he sent across what [belonged] to him.

en.L: He took them and sent them across the stream, and he sent across everything he had.
en.B: He took them and sent them over the stream, along with everything he owned.
en.R: He sent his family and everything he owned across the river.

es.L: Los tomó y les hizo cruzar el arroyo, e hizo pasar todo lo que tenía.
es.B: Los tomó y los hizo pasar al otro lado del torrente, junto con todo lo que poseía.
es.R: Hizo pasar el río a su familia y todo lo que tenía.

fr.L: Il les prit et leur fit passer le torrent, et il fit passer tout ce qui était à lui.
fr.B: Il les prit et leur fit traverser le torrent, avec tout ce qu’il possédait.
fr.R: Il a fait traverser la rivière à sa famille et à tout ce qu’il avait.

sw.L: Akawachukua, akawavusha kijito, akavusha pia vyote alivyokuwa navyo.

sw.R: Aliivusha jamaa yake na mali yake yote ng'ambo ya mto.

decisions.choice: stream: a wadi
decisions.reason: The word (nachal) means a valley with a stream that may run dry in summer. The Jabbok runs all year in a deep gorge.

source.text: וַיִּוָּתֵ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַיֵּאָבֵ֥ק אִישׁ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ עַ֖ד עֲל֥וֹת הַשָּֽׁחַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And was left Jacob by himself, and wrestled a man with him until [the] going up of the dawn.

en.L: And Jacob was left alone. And a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the dawn.
en.B: Jacob stayed behind by himself. And a man wrestled with him there until dawn began to break.
en.R: Now Jacob was alone. A man came and wrestled with him all night, until dawn.

es.L: Y Jacob se quedó solo. Y un hombre luchó con él hasta que rayó el alba.
es.B: Jacob se quedó atrás, solo. Y un hombre luchó con él allí hasta que empezó a despuntar el alba.
es.R: Ahora Jacob estaba solo. Un hombre vino y luchó con él toda la noche, hasta el amanecer.

fr.L: Et Jacob resta seul. Et un homme lutta avec lui jusqu’au lever de l’aurore.
fr.B: Jacob resta en arrière, tout seul. Et là, un homme lutta avec lui jusqu’à ce que l’aube commence à poindre.
fr.R: Jacob était maintenant seul. Un homme est venu et a lutté avec lui toute la nuit, jusqu’à l’aube.

sw.L: Yakobo akabaki peke yake. Na mtu mmoja akashikana naye mieleka mpaka kupambazuka kwa alfajiri.
sw.B: Yakobo alibaki nyuma peke yake. Mtu mmoja akashikana naye mieleka pale mpaka alfajiri ilipoanza kupambazuka.
sw.R: Sasa Yakobo alikuwa peke yake. Mtu mmoja akaja, akapigana naye mieleka usiku kucha mpaka mapambazuko.

decisions.choice: a man wrestled with him: who was he?
decisions.reason: The text says only "a man". In the end Jacob knows he has seen God face to face (verse 31). Hosea 12:4-5 calls him an angel: Jacob "strove with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought his favor". The text leaves the mystery in place.

decisions.choice: wrestled (ye'aveq)
decisions.reason: The verb is used only here and in verse 26; it may come from avaq, "dust", the dust raised by wrestlers. It sounds like Jabbok and Jacob (verse 23).

decisions.choice: Jacob alone
decisions.reason: Jacob has sent everyone and everything ahead. Before he meets Esau, he must meet God alone, as at Bethel when he was alone in flight (28:11).

source.text: וַיַּ֗רְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָכֹל֙ ל֔וֹ וַיִּגַּ֖ע בְּכַף־יְרֵכ֑וֹ וַתֵּ֨קַע֙ כַּף־יֶ֣רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּהֵֽאָבְק֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he saw that not he prevailed against him, and he touched [the] socket of his thigh; and was dislocated [the] socket of [the] thigh of Jacob as he wrestled with him.

en.L: And when the man saw that he did not prevail against him, he touched the socket of his hip, and the socket of Jacob's hip was wrenched as he wrestled with him.
en.B: The man, seeing that he could not get the upper hand over Jacob, struck him at the hip socket, and Jacob's hip was wrenched out of joint while they wrestled.
en.R: The man saw that he could not win the fight. So he touched Jacob's hip and put it out of joint as they wrestled.

es.L: Y cuando el hombre vio que no podía con él, le tocó la articulación de la cadera, y se dislocó la articulación de la cadera de Jacob mientras luchaba con él.
es.B: Al ver el hombre que no lograba vencer a Jacob, lo golpeó en la articulación de la cadera, y la cadera de Jacob se dislocó mientras forcejeaban.
es.R: El hombre vio que no podía ganar la pelea. Entonces le tocó la cadera a Jacob y se la dislocó mientras luchaban.

fr.L: Et quand l’homme vit qu’il ne l’emportait pas sur lui, il toucha l’emboîture de sa hanche, et l’emboîture de la hanche de Jacob se déboîta pendant qu’il luttait avec lui.
fr.B: Voyant qu’il ne parvenait pas à prendre le dessus sur Jacob, l’homme le frappa à l’articulation de la hanche, et la hanche de Jacob se déboîta pendant qu’ils luttaient.
fr.R: L’homme a vu qu’il ne pouvait pas gagner le combat. Alors il a touché la hanche de Jacob et la lui a déboîtée pendant qu’ils luttaient.

sw.L: Na yule mtu alipoona kwamba hamshindi, akamgusa kiungo cha nyonga yake; nacho kiungo cha nyonga ya Yakobo kikateguka alipokuwa akishikana naye mieleka.
sw.B: Yule mtu alipoona kwamba hawezi kumshinda Yakobo, alimpiga kwenye kiungo cha nyonga, na nyonga ya Yakobo ikateguka walipokuwa wakishikana mieleka.
sw.R: Yule mtu aliona kwamba hawezi kushinda. Kwa hiyo akaigusa nyonga ya Yakobo, nayo ikateguka walipokuwa wakipigana mieleka.

decisions.choice: he touched the socket of his hip: a touch that cripples
decisions.reason: A single touch is enough to put Jacob's hip out of joint. The man could have prevailed at any time; he lets Jacob wrestle. Jacob limps afterward (verse 32).

decisions.choice: wrenched: put out of joint
decisions.reason: The verb (yaqa) means to be dislocated or torn loose.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "he" is, since the Hebrew pronouns for the two wrestlers are easily confused.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שַׁלְּחֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י עָלָ֖ה הַשָּׁ֑חַר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֲשַֽׁלֵּחֲךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם־בֵּרַכְתָּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, let me go, for has gone up the dawn; and he said, not I will let you go unless you bless me.

en.L: Then he said, "Let me go, for the dawn has broken." But Jacob said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
en.B: "Let me go," said the man, "for the dawn is coming up." Jacob said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
en.R: Then the man said, "Let me go. The sun is coming up." But Jacob said, "I will not let you go until you bless me."

es.L: Entonces dijo: «Déjame ir, porque ha rayado el alba». Pero Jacob dijo: «No te dejaré ir si no me bendices».
es.B: «Déjame ir», dijo el hombre, «porque ya está amaneciendo». Jacob respondió: «No te dejaré ir a menos que me bendigas».
es.R: Entonces el hombre dijo: «Déjame ir. Ya está saliendo el sol». Pero Jacob le dijo: «No te dejaré ir hasta que me bendigas».

fr.L: Alors il dit : « Laisse-moi aller, car l’aurore s’est levée. » Mais Jacob dit : « Je ne te laisserai pas aller, à moins que tu ne me bénisses. »
fr.B: « Laisse-moi partir, dit l’homme, car l’aube se lève. » Jacob répondit : « Je ne te laisserai pas partir si tu ne me bénis pas. »
fr.R: Alors l’homme a dit : « Laisse-moi partir. Le soleil se lève. » Mais Jacob a dit : « Je ne te laisserai pas partir tant que tu ne m’auras pas béni. »

sw.L: Kisha akasema, "Niache niende, kwa maana alfajiri imepambazuka." Lakini Yakobo akasema, "Sitakuacha uende usiponibariki."
sw.B: "Niache niende," yule mtu akasema, "kwa maana kunapambazuka." Yakobo akasema, "Sitakuacha uende isipokuwa unibariki."
sw.R: Kisha yule mtu akasema, "Niache niende. Jua linachomoza." Lakini Yakobo akasema, "Sitakuacha mpaka unibariki."

decisions.choice: Let me go, for the dawn has broken
decisions.reason: The text does not say why the man must leave at dawn. It may be that Jacob must not see his face in daylight (compare Exodus 33:20). Jacob, who once took a blessing by deceit (27:35), now clings to this one and asks for it openly.

decisions.choice: me (no deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The man is called "a man" and speaks of God in the third person (verse 29), so his words are not given the deity pronoun setting, even though Jacob recognizes God in the meeting (verse 31).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו מַה־שְּׁמֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, what [is] your name? And he said, Jacob.

en.L: And he said to him, "What is your name?" And he said, "Jacob."
en.B: The man asked him, "What is your name?" He said, "Jacob."
en.R: The man asked him, "What is your name?" He answered, "Jacob."

es.L: Y le dijo: «¿Cuál es tu nombre?». Y él dijo: «Jacob».
es.B: El hombre le preguntó: «¿Cómo te llamas?». Él dijo: «Jacob».
es.R: El hombre le preguntó: «¿Cuál es tu nombre?». Él respondió: «Jacob».

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « Quel est ton nom ? » Et il dit : « Jacob. »
fr.B: L’homme lui demanda : « Comment t’appelles-tu ? » Il dit : « Jacob. »
fr.R: L’homme lui a demandé : « Quel est ton nom ? » Il a répondu : « Jacob. »

sw.L: Akamwambia, "Jina lako ni nani?" Akasema, "Yakobo."
sw.B: Yule mtu akamwuliza, "Unaitwa nani?" Akasema, "Yakobo."
sw.R: Yule mtu akamwuliza, "Jina lako ni nani?" Akajibu, "Yakobo."

decisions.choice: Jacob: the name of the heel-grabber
decisions.reason: The name Jacob was explained by "heel" (aqev) at his birth (25:26), and Esau took it to mean "he cheats" (27:36). When Isaac asked "Who are you?" Jacob had answered with Esau's name (27:18-19). Now he must say his own name, and with it, who he has been.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־שָׂרִ֧יתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִ֛ים וְעִם־אֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַתּוּכָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, not Jacob will be said again [as] your name, but Israel; for you have striven with God and with men and have prevailed.

en.L: And he said, "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed."
en.B: He said, "You will be called Jacob no longer. Your name is Israel, for you have contended with God and with people and have come through victorious."
en.R: Then the man said, "From now on your name will be Israel, which means 'he struggles with God.' It will not be Jacob anymore. You have struggled with God and with people, and you have won."

es.L: Y dijo: «Ya no se dirá Jacob tu nombre, sino Israel, porque has luchado con Dios y con los hombres, y has vencido».
es.B: Él dijo: «Ya no te llamarás Jacob. Tu nombre es Israel, porque has contendido con Dios y con los seres humanos, y has salido vencedor».
es.R: Entonces el hombre dijo: «De ahora en adelante te llamarás Israel, que significa “lucha con Dios”. Ya no te llamarás Jacob. Has luchado con Dios y con la gente, y has ganado».

fr.L: Et il dit : « On ne t’appellera plus du nom de Jacob, mais d’Israël, car tu as lutté avec Dieu et avec des hommes, et tu l’as emporté. »
fr.B: Il dit : « Tu ne t’appelleras plus Jacob. Ton nom est Israël, car tu as combattu avec Dieu et avec les humains, et tu en es sorti vainqueur. »
fr.R: Alors l’homme a dit : « À partir de maintenant, ton nom sera Israël, ce qui veut dire “il lutte avec Dieu”. Ce ne sera plus Jacob. Tu as lutté avec Dieu et avec les gens, et tu as gagné. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Jina lako halitaitwa tena Yakobo, bali Israeli, kwa maana umeshindana na Mungu na wanadamu, nawe umeshinda."
sw.B: Akasema, "Hutaitwa tena Yakobo. Jina lako ni Israeli, kwa sababu umepambana na Mungu na watu, nawe umeibuka mshindi."
sw.R: Kisha yule mtu akasema, "Tangu sasa jina lako litakuwa Israeli, maana yake 'anashindana na Mungu.' Halitakuwa Yakobo tena. Umeshindana na Mungu na watu, nawe umeshinda."

decisions.choice: Israel: "he strives with God", a pun on sarita, "you have striven"
decisions.reason: The name Israel sounds like the verb sarah, "strive" or "contend", with El, "God". As a name it may first mean "God strives" or "God rules"; the man explains it by Jacob's striving with God. Hosea 12:4 recalls the verse: "in his strength he strove with God".

decisions.choice: with God and with men, and have prevailed
decisions.reason: Jacob has contended with Esau and Laban, and now with God. He has "prevailed" (yakhol, as in Rachel's words in 30:8), not by overpowering God but by holding on for the blessing. The new name marks a new identity; God confirms it at Bethel (35:10).

decisions.choice: men: people
decisions.reason: The word (anashim) here means human beings in contrast with God: Esau, Laban and others.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "people", since the contrast is between God and human beings (m3). The men in question are named men, so no gender setting is used.

decisions.choice: which means 'he struggles with God'
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֣ל יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֣א שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה תִּשְׁאַ֣ל לִשְׁמִ֑י וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֹת֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And asked Jacob and said, tell please your name; and he said, why [is] this [that] you ask about my name? And he blessed him there.

en.L: And Jacob asked him and said, "Please tell me your name." But he said, "Why is it that you ask my name?" And there he blessed him.
en.B: Then Jacob asked him, "Tell me, please, what your name is." He replied, "Why is it that you ask for my name?" And there he blessed Jacob.
en.R: Then Jacob said, "Please tell me your name." But the man said, "Why do you want to know my name?" Then he blessed Jacob there.

es.L: Y Jacob le preguntó y dijo: «Dime, te ruego, tu nombre». Pero él dijo: «¿Por qué preguntas por mi nombre?». Y lo bendijo allí.
es.B: Entonces Jacob le pidió: «Dime, por favor, cuál es tu nombre». Él respondió: «¿Por qué me preguntas mi nombre?». Y allí bendijo a Jacob.
es.R: Después Jacob le dijo: «Por favor, dime tu nombre». Pero el hombre respondió: «¿Para qué quieres saber mi nombre?». Entonces bendijo a Jacob allí mismo.

fr.L: Et Jacob l’interrogea et dit : « Fais-moi connaître ton nom, je te prie. » Mais il dit : « Pourquoi donc demandes-tu mon nom ? » Et il le bénit là.
fr.B: Alors Jacob lui demanda : « Dis-moi, je t’en prie, quel est ton nom. » Il répondit : « Pourquoi me demandes-tu mon nom ? » Et là, il bénit Jacob.
fr.R: Puis Jacob a dit : « S’il te plaît, dis-moi ton nom. » Mais l’homme a répondu : « Pourquoi veux-tu savoir mon nom ? » Puis, à cet endroit, il a béni Jacob.

sw.L: Yakobo akamwuliza, akasema, "Tafadhali niambie jina lako." Lakini akasema, "Kwa nini waniuliza jina langu?" Akambariki pale.
sw.B: Kisha Yakobo akamwomba, "Tafadhali, niambie jina lako ni nani." Akajibu, "Kwa nini unaniuliza jina langu?" Na hapo akambariki Yakobo.
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo akasema, "Tafadhali niambie jina lako." Lakini yule mtu akasema, "Kwa nini unataka kujua jina langu?" Kisha akambariki Yakobo pale pale.

decisions.choice: Why do you ask my name?: the name withheld
decisions.reason: To know a name was to know a person's nature and, people thought, to have some hold on him. The man refuses, as the angel of the LORD later does to Manoah (Judges 13:17-18), but he gives the blessing Jacob asked for (verse 27).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֧א יַעֲקֹ֛ב שֵׁ֥ם הַמָּק֖וֹם פְּנִיאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־רָאִ֤יתִי אֱלֹהִים֙ פָּנִ֣ים אֶל־פָּנִ֔ים וַתִּנָּצֵ֖ל נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Jacob [the] name of the place Peniel, for I have seen God face to face, and has been delivered my life.

en.L: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel, "For I have seen God face to face, and yet my life has been spared."
en.B: Jacob named the place Peniel. "I have seen God face to face," he said, "and my life has been rescued."
en.R: Jacob named that place Peniel, which means "the face of God." He said, "I have seen God face to face, but I am still alive!"

es.L: Y llamó Jacob el nombre del lugar Peniel: «Porque he visto a Dios cara a cara, y aun así mi vida ha sido preservada».
es.B: Jacob llamó a aquel lugar Peniel. «He visto a Dios cara a cara», dijo, «y mi vida ha sido librada».
es.R: Jacob le puso a ese lugar el nombre de Peniel, que significa «la cara de Dios». Dijo: «¡He visto a Dios cara a cara, y todavía estoy vivo!».

fr.L: Et Jacob appela le nom du lieu Peniel : « Car j’ai vu Dieu face à face, et pourtant ma vie a été préservée. »
fr.B: Jacob nomma ce lieu Peniel. « J’ai vu Dieu face à face, dit-il, et ma vie a été sauvée. »
fr.R: Jacob a appelé cet endroit Peniel, ce qui veut dire « le visage de Dieu ». Il a dit : « J’ai vu Dieu face à face, et pourtant je suis encore vivant ! »

sw.L: Yakobo akapaita jina la mahali pale Penieli, "Kwa maana nimemwona Mungu uso kwa uso, na bado maisha yangu yamehifadhiwa."
sw.B: Yakobo akapaita mahali pale Penieli. "Nimemwona Mungu uso kwa uso," akasema, "na maisha yangu yameokolewa."
sw.R: Yakobo akapaita mahali pale Penieli, maana yake "uso wa Mungu." Akasema, "Nimemwona Mungu uso kwa uso, lakini bado ni mzima!"

decisions.choice: Peniel: "face of God"
decisions.reason: The name joins panim, "face", and El, "God". The next verse spells it Penuel, the form used later (Judges 8:8).

decisions.choice: seen God face to face and lived
decisions.reason: No one could see God's face and live (Exodus 33:20; Judges 6:22-23; 13:22). Jacob knows that the one he wrestled was God, and that he has been spared. He will say to Esau, "to see your face is like seeing the face of God" (33:10).

decisions.choice: which means "the face of God"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

source.text: וַיִּֽזְרַֽח־ל֣וֹ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָבַ֖ר אֶת־פְּנוּאֵ֑ל וְה֥וּא צֹלֵ֖עַ עַל־יְרֵכֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose for him the sun as he passed Penuel, and he [was] limping on his thigh.

en.L: And the sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel, limping because of his hip.
en.B: The sun was rising on him as he went past Penuel, and he went limping on his injured hip.
en.R: The sun came up as Jacob left Peniel. He was limping because of his hip.

es.L: Y le salió el sol cuando pasó Penuel, y cojeaba de su cadera.
es.B: El sol salía sobre él cuando pasó por Penuel, y caminaba cojeando de su cadera herida.
es.R: El sol salió cuando Jacob se iba de Peniel. Cojeaba por culpa de su cadera.

fr.L: Et le soleil se leva sur lui quand il passa Penuel, et il boitait à cause de sa hanche.
fr.B: Le soleil se levait sur lui quand il dépassa Penuel ; il boitait de sa hanche blessée.
fr.R: Le soleil s’est levé au moment où Jacob quittait Peniel. Il boitait à cause de sa hanche.

sw.L: Jua likamchomozea alipopita Penueli, naye alikuwa akichechemea kwa sababu ya nyonga yake.
sw.B: Jua lilikuwa likimchomozea alipopita Penueli, naye akaenda akichechemea kwa nyonga yake iliyoumia.
sw.R: Jua lilichomoza Yakobo alipokuwa akiondoka Penieli. Alikuwa akichechemea kwa sababu ya nyonga yake.

decisions.choice: the sun rose upon him
decisions.reason: When Jacob fled, "the sun had set" at Bethel (28:11). Now, as he returns, the sun rises on him. He goes on blessed, but limping.

decisions.choice: Penuel: another spelling of Peniel
decisions.reason: The two forms of the name differ by one vowel letter and mean the same thing.

decisions.choice: Peniel
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the spelling of verse 31 so that young readers see one place (m2).

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא־יֹאכְל֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־גִּ֣יד הַנָּשֶׁ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־כַּ֣ף הַיָּרֵ֔ךְ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֤י נָגַע֙ בְּכַף־יֶ֣רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּגִ֖יד הַנָּשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore not eat [the] sons of Israel the sinew of the thigh which [is] on [the] socket of the thigh until this day, because he touched [the] socket of [the] thigh of Jacob on the sinew of the thigh.

en.L: Therefore to this day the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the socket of the thigh, because he touched the socket of Jacob's thigh on the sinew of the hip.
en.B: This is the reason the people of Israel still do not eat the sinew on the hip socket: Jacob's hip socket was struck at that sinew.
en.R: That is why the people of Israel, even today, will not eat the muscle on the hip. The man touched Jacob's hip there.

es.L: Por eso, hasta el día de hoy, los hijos de Israel no comen el tendón de la cadera, que está sobre la articulación del muslo, porque él tocó la articulación del muslo de Jacob en el tendón de la cadera.
es.B: Esta es la razón por la que los israelitas todavía no comen el tendón de la articulación de la cadera: la cadera de Jacob fue golpeada en ese tendón.
es.R: Por eso, aun hoy, los israelitas no comen el músculo de la cadera. El hombre tocó la cadera de Jacob en ese lugar.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, jusqu’à ce jour, les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ne mangent pas le nerf de la hanche, qui est sur l’emboîture de la cuisse, parce qu’il toucha l’emboîture de la cuisse de Jacob au nerf de la hanche.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi, aujourd’hui encore, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ne mangent pas le nerf situé à l’articulation de la hanche : c’est à ce nerf que la hanche de Jacob fut frappée.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que, même aujourd’hui, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ne mangent pas le muscle de la hanche. C’est à cet endroit que l’homme a touché la hanche de Jacob.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo hata leo wana wa Israeli hawali mshipa wa nyonga ulio juu ya kiungo cha paja, kwa sababu alikigusa kiungo cha paja la Yakobo kwenye mshipa wa nyonga.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo sababu Waisraeli hata leo hawali mshipa ulio kwenye kiungo cha nyonga: nyonga ya Yakobo ilipigwa kwenye mshipa huo.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu hata leo Waisraeli hawali msuli wa nyonga. Yule mtu aligusa nyonga ya Yakobo mahali hapo.

decisions.choice: the sinew of the hip (gid hanasheh)
decisions.reason: The phrase seems to mean the long nerve or tendon that runs down the thigh, the sciatic nerve. The exact sense of nasheh is not known.

decisions.choice: to this day: a food custom of Israel
decisions.reason: The narrator explains an Israelite custom by Jacob's wrestling. It is not one of the laws given through Moses; it is a custom remembered from this event.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Here, for the first time, "sons of Israel" means the people descended from Jacob, now named Israel.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "people of Israel" for the nation descended from Jacob (m3).

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Readable says who touched Jacob's hip.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël (L); les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} (B, R)
alternatives: les fils d'Israël, with no setting, as the English
decisions.reason: The settled Pentateuch wording for the sons of Israel as a people. The English has no gender span here, but French has two real wordings: an inclusive default and the traditional "fils d'Israël" as the alternative.
